---
name: read-tree-goes-stale-between-add-and-commit
description: A private index seeded from HEAD becomes a deletion bomb if HEAD advances before you commit; the guard's "re-seed and re-add" is the fix, not a failure
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The fresh-private-index discipline (`rm -f`, `read-tree HEAD`, `add` explicit paths, verify stat, commit — all under `GIT_INDEX_FILE`) protects other lanes from *you*. It does not protect you from **time**. If another lane commits between your `read-tree` and your `commit`, your index still describes the *old* HEAD, so every path that lane added now reads as a staged **deletion** — and your pre-commit stat looked clean because you ran it before their commit landed.

**How it presented:** my staged stat showed exactly my 6 intended paths and zero `D` lines. The commit was then *rejected* by the workspace deletion guard, and the `show HEAD --stat` I ran afterwards displayed **another lane's four files** (a new AJCR chart file, two Albanese files) — because HEAD had moved and my post-commit check was reading their commit, not mine.

**Why:** `add`ing a path writes that path's blob into the index; everything else in the index is whatever `read-tree` put there. The index has no idea HEAD advanced.

**How to apply:** treat the whole four-step sequence as needing to be *short*, and when the guard refuses, do exactly what it says — make a **new** index file, `read-tree HEAD` again, re-`add` only your paths, commit. Do not set `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` to push past it; that is the flag that turns this into another lane's lost work. Do not reuse the stale index. And read the post-commit `--stat` for *filenames*, not just counts: seeing paths you never touched is the signal, whether they appear as additions or deletions ([[commit-stat-names-files-you-never-touched]]).
